page: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Allocated via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs spanning 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory footprint totals 256.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector acceleration is supported through AVX-512 extensions, including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Integrated directly into the instance is 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, offering low-latency scratch disk capabilities without requiring external volumes. The instance does not include a dedicated GPU accelerator, relying entirely on the x86_64 CPU subsystem for compute requirements.

Benchmark results place the D64ads_v7 in the top tier (top 10%) for single-core stress-ng workloads, PassMark CPU scores, and PassMark extended instruction execution. Memory throughput is strong, exceeding 205.9 GB/sec on uncached 256MB reads and 132.81 GB/sec on writes. In data-intensive evaluations, the VM achieves top-tier results in PassMark database operations and over 102 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. CPU-based machine learning inference performs in the top tier for lightweight and mid-sized models, though 70B parameter models settle into the middle 50% category due to memory bandwidth constraints inherent to general-purpose CPU architectures.

By coupling 64 high-clocked vCPUs, 256.0 GB of RAM, and high-capacity NVMe ephemeral storage, Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 offers solid resource density for database management, large-scale Redis caching, data analytics pipelines, and multi-threaded web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 256.0 GB of system memory, and 3780 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 platform supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI, without dedicated GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the instance achieves top 10% ratings in PassMark CPU, database operations, and single-core stress-ng tests, alongside strong performance in large-block memory transfers and Redis operations. The local high-speed NVMe storage and balanced memory ratio make it well aligned for database hosting, caching layers, data processing, and enterprise web-tier applications.
